title: Terms from founder life, briefly explained.
intro: A focused glossary for terms you encounter while building a startup and working as a founder.
professionalNote: For legal or tax questions, the Library is not a substitute for individual professional advice.
setupPrompt: Relevant to your team right now?

bootstrapping.shortDefinition: Building a company primarily with the founders’ own resources and operating revenue rather than external equity financing.

burn_rate.shortDefinition: The amount of cash a company uses on a net basis over a given period, often measured monthly.

cap_table.shortDefinition: A record of who owns which shares or other equity interests in a company.

deadlock.shortDefinition: A decision-making stalemate in which the agreed voting rules or responsibilities cannot produce an outcome.

dilution.shortDefinition: The reduction in an existing stakeholder’s percentage ownership when new shares are issued.

drag_along_tag_along.shortDefinition: Contractual rules for the sale of company shares: drag-along can require certain shareholders to join a sale under defined conditions; tag-along can give other shareholders the right to participate in another shareholder’s sale on comparable terms.

esop_vsop.shortDefinition: Employee participation models: An ESOP typically uses actual shares or options for actual shares. A VSOP contractually mirrors an equity interest without directly creating shareholder status.

founder_agreement.shortDefinition: An agreement between founders that records central rules about their collaboration, ownership, and possible changes.

founder_exit.shortDefinition: A founder leaving the operating team, the company’s ownership structure, or both, with possible consequences for roles and equity.

good_bad_leaver.shortDefinition: Contractual categories for different ways of leaving a company that may carry different consequences for equity rights.

ip_assignment.shortDefinition: Contractual arrangements through which intellectual property rights or corresponding rights of use – such as rights in code, designs, trademarks, or inventions – are assigned to a company.

mvp.shortDefinition: A Minimum Viable Product is a deliberately limited first product version used to test core assumptions with real users.

pivot.shortDefinition: A fundamental change in product, business model, or target market based on new evidence.

pre_money_post_money.shortDefinition: Pre-money is a company’s valuation before a financing round; post-money includes the newly invested capital.

product_market_fit.shortDefinition: The point at which a product meets a meaningful market need well enough for sustained demand to become evident.

reverse_vesting.shortDefinition: An arrangement where shares have already been transferred but may remain subject to repurchase or retransfer rights that reduce over time.

runway.shortDefinition: The estimated time a company can continue operating with its available cash at its current rate of spending.

term_sheet.shortDefinition: A summary of the main proposed terms of an investment or financing before the detailed agreements are drafted.

vesting.shortDefinition: A mechanism that defines the period over which equity rights are gradually treated as earned or non-forfeitable and what consequences an early departure may have.

convertible_loan.shortDefinition: A loan whose repayment claim is converted, or can be converted, into equity under agreed conditions.
